clue.text: Nerve-racking as fuel turns explosive

indicators.note: explosive suggests the words fuel and turns are blown apart and their letters scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fuel churning around in a way that could blow up at any moment is a nerve-racking business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder: FUEL and TURNS together give the nine letters, and 'explosive' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nerve-racking gives no peace or calm, which is what being without rest describes.

clue.text: Prepare to take in washing?

parts.note: before laundry drying on a line can be brought indoors, the clips holding each item must be removed

explanation.definitionFit: Taking clothes off a line means removing the clothes-pegs first, a playful verb for undoing that fastening.

clue.text: Embarrassed about raising issue moved in schedule

indicators.note: about means the word for embarrassed is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: embarrassed people go red in the face

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means reading it from the bottom upwards, so it runs backwards

parts.note: issue means offspring, and a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: Someone blushing about a contentious matter that has been pushed to a different slot in the timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' suggests a topic under discussion, but it means offspring; 'raising' turns the child word upwards in this down clue, giving ETIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given a new slot in a timetable has had its timing altered.

clue.text: Shot! — three instead of four?

definitions.meaning: a cricket stroke played square of the wicket on the off side, hitting a short ball away
a four-sided figure sliced across its diagonal leaves a three-sided shape

explanation.walkthrough: A SQUARE CUT is a cricket stroke; read literally, cutting a square corner to corner leaves triangles, three sides instead of four.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this is a named batting stroke; literally, slicing a four-sided figure produces three-sided pieces.

clue.text: Missed one's footing, taking this outdoor exercise?

definitions.text: Missed one's footing, taking this outdoor exercise?

parts.words: Missed one's footing, taking this outdoor exercise?
parts.note: read as two words, the activity describes someone who toppled over while out on a stroll, as well as hiking in hill country

explanation.walkthrough: Fells are the hills of northern England; the hobby of hiking over them, read as a sentence, says someone tumbled while on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiking across the upland moors of northern England is a recognised outdoor pastime, and the phrase also reads as tumbling mid-stroll.

clue.text: Got all behind

parts.note: a person at the front of a procession or race has everyone else trailing in their wake

explanation.definitionFit: Being out in front of the pack, so everyone else follows, is what heading a race means.

clue.text: More leaky-sounding pigment

indicators.note: sounding means the word for more leaky is said out loud and heard as another word

parts.note: something that seeps more than another is seepier

explanation.surface: A paint colour that oozes through its container more than others do.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the reddish-brown colouring originally made from cuttlefish ink, used for old photographs.

clue.text: Appeal to girl to have bath

parts.note: SA is short for sex appeal
Una is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Making a request to a young woman so that she can take a soak.
explanation.walkthrough: SA for sex appeal is a crossword convention, as is a short girl's name like UNA.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauna is a steam bath, a hot room where people sit and sweat.

clue.text: Keeping it in force not entirely advisable

indicators.note: keeping means the shortened police word holds the other piece inside it
not entirely means the last letter of the word for force is dropped

parts.note: the police are often called the force
taken as written

explanation.surface: Retaining something in effect is only partly a sensible course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'force' reads as compulsion, but it is the usual nickname for the police; 'not entirely' drops its last letter, leaving POLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Politic means prudent or shrewd, a wise course in the circumstances.

clue.text: Creature with hard top, or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters of hard top and or are arranged differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An animal with a tough shell on its back, or something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with hard top' looks like part of a description of a crab, but HARDTOP plus OR is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An arthropod is an invertebrate animal with jointed legs and an exoskeleton, such as an insect or crab.

clue.text: Dog's mine? Rubbish!

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
bull is slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone claims the dog belongs to them, and another person scoffs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like a possessive claiming the dog, but it is a coal mine.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a breed of muscular fighting terrier.

clue.text: Pairing takes time to bid

indicators.note: to here means the letter for time is attached at the end of the bid word

parts.note: in bridge, a double is a call made in the bidding

explanation.surface: Matching people up is a slow business before an offer can be made.
explanation.walkthrough: In the card game bridge, DOUBLE is a call in the auction, so it counts as a bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet is a couple of matching things, such as two identical words or dice faces.

clue.text: More handicapped player using computer

definitions.meaning: game is an old word for lame, so this is the comparative, lamer

explanation.definitionFit: Game once meant lame in the leg, so more lame is this comparative; it is also a person who plays video games.

clue.text: Composer engages pole as site manager

indicators.note: engages means the composer's name takes hold of the other piece inside it

parts.note: Carl Maria von Weber was a German composer
a mast is a tall pole

explanation.surface: A musician takes on a flagpole to run a building site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'site manager' suggests a building site, but it is a website.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who runs a website is in charge of the site, a modern sense of manager.

clue.text: Showing boob on public transport, say, one was fired

indicators.note: on means in this down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a boob is a mistake

indicators.note: say indicates the word for public transport is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: Someone makes a gaffe on the bus and loses their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one was fired' reads as a sacking, but it is an old gun; BUSS (a kiss) sounds like bus.
explanation.definitionFit: This was an old short-barrelled firearm with a flared muzzle, so it was a weapon that was shot.

clue.text: Acted, but dried regularly

indicators.note: regularly means picking every other letter of the word dried, starting with the first

explanation.surface: An actor performed, but kept forgetting their lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dried' suggests the theatrical sense of forgetting lines, matching 'Acted', but it is only the source of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Did is the past tense of do, which means performed or carried out an action.

clue.text: Impervious barrier almost silently installed on top of house

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across a river
PP, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quietly, close to silence
a roof is fitted on top of a house

explanation.surface: A barrier against water being quietly fitted on a house.
explanation.walkthrough: PP is the musical marking pianissimo, very softly, so 'almost silently'.
explanation.definitionFit: Impervious here means resistant to moisture, as a damp-proof course is.

clue.text: Here lots of Indians bowl in annual match

parts.note: Calcutta (Kolkata) is a large Indian city where many Indians live
a cup is a bowl-shaped vessel

explanation.surface: A place where many Indian cricketers bowl during a yearly fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indians' and 'bowl' suggest cricket, but the match is rugby union, played every year between England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: This trophy is contested every year in the rugby union fixture between England and Scotland.

clue.text: Debtor happy at first until taken out to place of execution

indicators.note: taken out means the word for until is stretched open to hold the other pieces

parts.note: till means until
someone who owes is an ower

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of happy is used

explanation.surface: A debtor is cheerful at first until marched off to be beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken out' signals the until word stretched open to hold the others. Tower Hill, beside the Tower of London, was a site of public beheadings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tower Hill, outside the Tower of London, was where prisoners were publicly beheaded.

clue.text: "Out, damn' wine!" — pouring this?

indicators.note: pouring suggests the letters flow out of the quoted words and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A drinker spurns the wine while pouring something stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: MOUNTAIN DEW is a name for illicit Scotch or Irish whisky, so someone damning wine might pour it instead.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a slang name for illicitly distilled whisky, a spirit one might pour instead of wine.

clue.text: Source of power university briefly expanded

definitions.meaning: a radioactive element used as nuclear fuel
U is the short form of university, and the same letter is the chemical symbol of an element; written out in full it gives that element's name

explanation.walkthrough: University abbreviates to U, which is also the chemical symbol for the nuclear fuel element; expanding that symbol spells out the element's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This radioactive metal fuels nuclear reactors, so it is a source of energy; its chemical symbol is U.

clue.text: Bloke put back arrival day

indicators.note: put back means the letters for arrival day are turned round

parts.note: DOB is short for date of birth, the day you arrived in the world

explanation.surface: A man postponed the day he was due to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: BOD is British slang for a person, usually a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Bod is British slang for a chap or person.

clue.text: Extremist characters come in to reserve a powerful weapon

indicators.note: come in to means the extremist letters enter the word for reserve

parts.note: to book is to reserve
A and Z are the letters at either extreme of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Radicals arrive to stockpile a dangerous weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremist' suggests radicals, but it means the extremes of the alphabet, A and Z.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazooka is a portable anti-tank rocket launcher, a heavy weapon.

clue.text: Little Aussie's strong feeling after mate swipes husband

indicators.note: after means the strong feeling comes after the first piece
swipes means the word for mate grabs the husband letter and holds it

parts.note: a pal is a mate
anger is a strong feeling

explanation.surface: An Australian is furious after his friend steals her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Aussie' suggests a person, but it is a small Australian marsupial.
explanation.definitionFit: A phalanger is a small tree-dwelling marsupial of Australia, such as a possum.

clue.text: A sign from heaven god has accepted one?

indicators.note: has accepted means the god's name takes the letter for one inside it

parts.note: Ares is the Greek god of war
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A divine omen: the god has taken someone in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign from heaven' suggests an omen, but it is a sign of the zodiac in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the Ram, is one of the twelve zodiac signs, constellations in the sky.

clue.text: Cutter runs to Portuguese islands, two points adrift

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: adrift means the two compass letters have floated away from the islands' name

parts.note: the Azores are an Atlantic archipelago belonging to Portugal
E and S are two points of the compass

explanation.surface: A boat races to the Azores but drifts a couple of points off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutter' suggests a sailing boat, which suits the voyage, but it is a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A razor is a blade used for shaving, so it is something that cuts.

clue.text: What may involve fit — installing new cooker

indicators.note: installing means the letter for new is fitted inside the other word

parts.note: rage can involve a fit, as in a fit of rage

explanation.surface: Fitting a new kitchen appliance may bring on a tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: A RANGE is a large kitchen stove.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a large kitchen stove with several hotplates and ovens.

clue.text: Don't die, drinking popular mineral

indicators.note: drinking means the plea swallows the popular word inside it

parts.note: the exclamation O live! is a plea to someone not to die
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to stay alive by drinking a fashionable mineral water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't die' is read as the plea 'O live!', which takes IN inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivine is a green silicate rock-forming mineral.

clue.text: Be very keen to get up for festival

indicators.note: in a down clue, get up means the word is read from the bottom so it runs backwards

parts.note: to be dying to do something is to be very keen

explanation.surface: Eager to rise early for a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: EID is a Muslim festival, as in Eid al-Fitr.
explanation.definitionFit: Eid is a major Muslim celebration, such as the one marking the end of Ramadan.

clue.text: College meal that's fabulous

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
corn ground up makes meal, as in cornmeal

explanation.surface: Dinner at university is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' looks like praise, but it means belonging to fable.
explanation.definitionFit: The unicorn is a creature of legend, so it is found in fables.

clue.text: Smoke gets me into no end of trouble

indicators.note: into means the word me is put inside the shortened trouble word
no end of means the last letter of the trouble word is removed

parts.note: fuss means bother or trouble
taken as written

explanation.surface: Smoking gets me into endless difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of' looks like 'lots of', but it drops the last S of FUSS, leaving FUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Fumes are smoky gas or vapour.

clue.text: Upset to find place in grip of flu, say

indicators.note: in grip of means the abbreviation for place is held inside the illness word

parts.note: flu is an example of a disease

explanation.surface: Being stuck somewhere with influenza is upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks flu as an example of a DISEASE, not a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: To displease someone is to annoy or upset them.
